scope: Refine six Fujifilm capture covers for grid harmony; preserve both Classic covers, Portra and collection originals

images.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: ONE square flat film-package front-panel cover used at 110px in a 3-column camera app grid.
Input image 1 is the edit target. Input image 2 is the existing nine-cover app grid, for palette balance and family context only. Produce only this ONE cover, not a sheet or app screenshot.
Primary request: refine this researched packaging adaptation into a calmer, harmonious collectible film-cover family. Preserve the stock identity, original product typography and signature packaging motifs/colors. Reduce competing text sizes and color intensity. It must look thoughtfully composed next to the two existing Classic covers and Portra, rather than shouting over them.
SHARED FAMILY RULES:
- Brand header occupies exactly the top 14% of the canvas, in printed Fujifilm green with less glare than the current target (around #148348, clearly green, not neon, not gray). Small ivory-white FUJIFILM logo at x=7%, y=4%, logo width about 35%, height about 5%. Preserve red detail in the logo. Header label remains subordinate.
- Only ONE dominant typographic element: the film's product name, placed within the central region y=37%-61%, optically centered. Title height around 15%-19% of the whole canvas, width at most 82%, safe side margins 7% minimum. Name should be the first thing the eye reads. Keep stock-specific lettering style. Never make a speed number compete with the name.
- FUJICHROME/FUJICOLOR/NEOPAN as appropriate is a small category line above the name, 3%-4% cap-height. The word Professional if present is only a tiny secondary descriptor, never a large independent stripe.
- Speed/format marks are a quiet footer: 50, 100F, 100 II or 120 no taller than 6%-7% of the canvas. All secondary technical text at the same baseline, bottom safe margin 7%; avoid a stack of huge numbers.
- Broader, calmer color fields, ample intentional breathing space around the name, fewer horizontal divisions (at most 3 main color regions, excluding thin rules). Existing characteristic banner/tab/diagonal may be retained at restrained scale.
- Shared matte printed-ink palette: warm ivory instead of brilliant white, charcoal instead of pure black, slightly softened stock-identification hues rather than electric RGB colors. Retain confident saturated key colors, not a desaturated brown/vintage wash. Fine almost invisible paper grain, no large mottling, no glare or gradients.
- Full-bleed orthographic 1:1 square panel. No margins outside the panel, no rounded corners or cast shadow, no 3D box sides, cartridge, photographic scene, collage, UI, border frame or watermark.
- Exact product text, no invented copy. Do not print JustShoot, RAW, sRGB, arrows or slogans. Never change the stock name. Do not redesign the entire collection into an identical generic template: retain each stock's distinctive label geometry and lettering while following the common scale and spacing.
PROVIA-specific: keep the elegant serif PROVIA and blue/gold/black professional-film identity. Below the green header, use deep printed royal blue (#233B83 approximately) as one uninterrupted large field down to y=78%, with a calm charcoal footer below y=78%. PROVIA in muted pale gold (#E5CE83) centered around y=48%, thin pale-gold rule immediately above/below the TITLE area only, not many bands. Small FUJICHROME above the title; small italic Professional below it. Small 100F at bottom-left of the charcoal footer, tiny technical info at bottom-right. Crucially REMOVE the huge 100F and huge Professional from the target. Palette should be deep blue with warm pale gold, not glowing electric blue/yellow.
Text verbatim: "FUJIFILM", "FUJICHROME", "PROVIA", "Professional", "100F", "35mm · 36EXP", "ISO 100 · E-6".
